raw_case_text:
The index case was a 53-year old woman with acute renal failure, who had elevated serum creatinine of 380.7mumol/L (reference 44.2-132.6mumol/L), positive ANCA against myeoperoxidase and biopsy-confirmed type III crescentic glomerulonephritis. Besides four sessions of plasmapheresis, she was treated for ANCA-associated renal vasculitis with daily intravenous mythelprednisolone of 320mg for three consecutive days and 40mg thereafter. Free of pulmonary infection (PI) (Figure 1), the patient was discharged one month later with a daily oral dose of 40mg mythelprednisolone.
Readmission occurred seven days post hoc due to fever (38.6 C) and hemoptysis. CT scan on admission (Day 1) found PI with cavitation. Laboratory tests showed WBC count 20.3x109/L with 96.9% neutrophils, T-lymphocyte count 102/uL (690-1760/uL), hemoglobin 110g/L (130-150g/L), platelet 170x109/L (100-300x109/L), C-reaction protein 185.2mg/L (<10mg/L), calcitonin 1.6ng/mL (<0.05ng/mL), (1,3)-beta glucan D detection test (G-test) 67.8pg/mL (<10pg/mL), serum creatinine 300.0umol/L, normal coagulation function including D-dimer and negative ANCA. Aerobic sputum but not blood cultures produced aeruginosa. She was immediately given intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics with dose and form respectively determined by creatinine clearance and CT findings (Figure 1): meropenem and voriconazole (Day 1 to 8), piperacillin sodium/tazobactam sodium and voriconazole with double-dose (Day 9 to 14), cefoperazone/sulbactam and micafungi (Day 15 to 19). The use of steroid was continued but reduced to half-dose two days after admission. Meanwhile, recurrent hypernatremia emerged (150-170mmol/L) which was only remedial to blood purification. There was sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis, prompting the collection of blood and sputum from deep trachea for specific microbial tests by our pharmacological center, which is a reliable and sophisticated research institution. In short notice thereafter, brain abscess was detected by MRI (Figure 2). The patient's condition further worsened and her vitals were no longer sustainable (Day 20). After that, growth of Nocardia asteroids from the said sputum was found on the Loewenstein-Jensen media and subsequently confirmed by the 16S rDNA sequence analysis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 53-year-old woman with MPO-ANCA-associated crescentic glomerulonephritis on high-dose methylprednisolone presented 7 days after hospital discharge with acute fever (38.6 C) and hemoptysis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One month after starting intensive immunosuppression (four sessions of plasmapheresis, IV methylprednisolone 320 mg/day for 3 days then 40 mg/day) for biopsy-proven type III crescentic glomerulonephritis and 7 days after being discharged on oral methylprednisolone 40 mg/day, the patient was readmitted with fever (38.6 C) and hemoptysis. During hospitalization, she developed refractory hypernatremia (150-170 mmol/L) and acute-onset aphasia and right hemiparesis.
subjective.past_medical_history: MPO-ANCA-positive type III crescentic glomerulonephritis with acute renal failure (baseline creatinine 380.7 umol/L, reference 44.2-132.6 umol/L) diagnosed 5 weeks prior and treated with plasmapheresis and high-dose methylprednisolone.
subjective.review_of_systems: Home medication: oral methylprednisolone 40 mg daily.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile at 38.6 C on admission; subsequently developed sudden-onset aphasia and right hemiparesis prior to hemodynamic collapse on hospital day 20.
objective.routine_investigations: Readmission labs (day 1) showed leukocytosis with WBC 20.3 x 10^9/L (96.9% neutrophils), hemoglobin 110 g/L (reference: 130-150 g/L), platelets 170 x 10^9/L (reference: 100-300 x 10^9/L), CRP 185.2 mg/L (reference: <10 mg/L), procalcitonin 1.6 ng/mL (reference: <0.05 ng/mL), serum creatinine 300.0 umol/L, normal coagulation/D-dimer, and negative ANCA; serum (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (G-test) was elevated at 67.8 pg/mL (reference: <10 pg/mL). Aerobic sputum culture initially grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa; blood cultures were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: T-lymphocyte count was severely depressed at 102/uL (reference: 690-1,760/uL). Day-1 chest CT demonstrated cavitary pulmonary infection. Following acute onset of aphasia and right hemiparesis, brain MRI revealed a cerebral abscess.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated (cavitary pulmonary and cerebral abscess) nocardiosis caused by Nocardia asteroides (with concomitant Pseudomonas aeruginosa respiratory infection) in a steroid-treated ANCA-vasculitis patient was confirmed post-mortem when deep tracheal sputum cultured on Lowenstein-Jensen media grew Nocardia asteroides, verified by 16S rDNA sequencing. During hospitalization, she had received sequential empirical regimens adjusted for renal function—meropenem plus voriconazole (days 1-8), piperacillin-tazobactam plus double-dose voriconazole (days 9-14), and cefoperazone-sulbactam plus micafungin (days 15-19)—alongside 50% steroid dose reduction and continuous blood purification for severe hypernatremia, but died on hospital day 20 before Nocardia culture confirmation.
